# WagerTech: Jira (WAGR) vs Meeting Transcripts — Variance Report

**Classification:** Internal / Client-Confidential. Not for client distribution.  
**Run date:** 2026-10-04  
**Window covered:** 27 May 2026 (Salesforce PRD Review) to 2026-10-04  
**Model used:** Claude (orchestrator: claude-fable-5-1; extraction, matching and verification subagents: Claude Opus 5.5, high effort)  
**Prepared for:** Miko Sumagang (Jumpr) — ramp-up on WagerTech  

## 1. Executive summary

After verification, 184 variances stay in the report: 2 High, 34 Medium and 148 Low (196 found, 6 rejected by verifiers, 6 folded as duplicates). Most are documentation drift, not build errors: 66 are decided items with no Jira ticket and 40 are tickets with stale text, and verifiers downgraded 69 of the 106 checked items that remain. The 2 High items are WAGR-271 (Done) letting Reps unarchive Sign-Ups when the client decided only Ops can (VAR-153), and no ticket or checklist for the production deployment at go-live (VAR-175).

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| High | 2 |

|---|---|---|

**Top High variances**

- **VAR-153** (V2, Access & Permissions / Org Setup): WAGR-271 (Done) lets Reps reactivate archived Sign-Ups, but the client decided that only Ops can unarchive — Jira: WAGR-271
- **VAR-175** (V1, Testing, UAT & Go-Live): No ticket for the production deployment of sandbox-built work, and no go-live deployment checklist (epic WAGR-18 is empty) — Jira: no ticket

**Patterns**

- Project Mgmt / Timeline: the go-live date or plan was replaced in 8 different meetings between 27 May and 13 Aug before 1 Nov was confirmed on 25 Sep, but WAGR-15, WAGR-17 and WAGR-23 still carry July and August dates (VAR-187), and no ticket covers the production deployment for go-live (VAR-175).
- Storage / Proofs: the storage direction changed in 7 meetings (13 superseded statements, 27 May to 4 Aug) and has been on hold since 25 Aug, yet WAGR-112 and WAGR-31 still say approved to proceed (VAR-168) and WAGR-32 is Done although the storage build was never delivered (VAR-169); this area has 6 variances.
- Deal has the most variances of any area (23, of which 10 are stale tickets): commercial-terms history changed in 3 meetings (11, 17 and 21 Sep) before the 30 Sep design, and WAGR-462 lacks the 30 Sep rules (VAR-033), WAGR-98 still leans to edit-in-place (VAR-031) and WAGR-13 still keys duplicates on Version (VAR-041).
- Gaps: Redeposits has the most decided items with no ticket, 15 of the 66 V1 gaps, including the redeposit data model, allocation date ranges, BA edit limits and incomplete-redeposit outcomes (VAR-081, VAR-083, VAR-086, VAR-087), ahead of Training & Enablement with 7 (VAR-177, VAR-180) and Operator & Partner and Reporting & Dashboards with 6 each.
- Verifier outcomes: of the 83 first-pass Medium items still in the report, verifiers downgraded 53 to Low, and 36 of those 53 reasons say a newer or umbrella ticket already tracks or partly covers the item, such as WAGR-464 for Redeposits (VAR-082, VAR-084) and WAGR-465 for Referral and Payouts (VAR-103, VAR-106); so most of the risk is stale or incomplete ticket text, not a wrong build.

## 2. Method and coverage

- **Transcripts read in full (Tier 1, client/project meetings):** 47 docs, 2749 extracted items. Each was read start to end by an extractor and re-read by an independent completeness critic.
- **Tier 2 (Jumpr-internal delivery-team meetings outside the two source folders, screened under rule 5):** 47 included / 5 excluded after reading; 712 items. Tier 2 items are used as corroboration or leads, never as the sole basis for a High/Medium variance.
- **Empty placeholders (1,180-byte docs; export is a byte-order mark only):** 8 — 2026-09-08 Wagertech Internal Sync; 2026-09-10 Wagertech Internal Sync; 2026-09-11 Wagertech Internal Sync; 2026-09-16 Wagertech <> Jumpr: Redeposits Discovery; 2026-09-22 Wagertech Internal Sync; 2026-09-29 Wagertech Internal Sync; 2026-10-02 Wagertech Internal Sync; 2026-10-02 Wagertech <> Jumpr: CMS Integration Sync. Plus 30 Sep Internal Sync (51-second recording, no content).
- **Duplicates/mirrors noted and removed:** 165 doc copies (shared-drive mirrors, Kobi-owned originals, 'Copy of' files). The 25 Aug Weekly Sync has 3 copies in the WagerTech subfolder; the largest was kept.
- **Docs excluded:** 31 non-transcript WagerTech docs (PRD, SOW, design plans, build walkthrough docs, specs, checklists) and 9 Jumpr-internal meetings with no separable WagerTech delivery content (see Appendix B).
- **Meetings with no transcript at all (Calendar cross-check, Kobi's and Miko's calendars):** 20 Jul 2026 'Wagertech <> Jumpr: Deal Rep Assignment' (5 attendees, no notes doc); 16 Sep 2026 Redeposits Discovery (placeholder only); 16 Jun 'Wagertech prep' and 1 Oct 'Waleed <> Kobi' (internal, no doc). 15 other calendar entries are single-attendee focus blocks. 40 of 58 calendar-attached Gemini originals are not shared with miko@; folder copies were used instead.
- **Jira:** all 505 WAGR issues pulled in full (fields, custom fields, links, all 493 comments) on 2026-10-03; 326 not Done. Key gaps WAGR-126/128/129/394/442 do not exist.
- **Verification:** every High and Medium variance (95) and a 20% sample of Low (21, every 5th) were re-checked by an independent verifier that re-fetched the Google Doc and the live Jira issue: 116 claims checked — confirmed 38, downgraded 72 (High→Medium 4, Medium→Low 55, same severity with lower confidence or narrower claim 12), rejected 6. 6 duplicate reports (same finding from both matching lenses) were folded into their primary. 78 Low variances were outside the sample and carry the finder's evidence only. Severity and confidence shown everywhere in this report are the post-verification values.
- **Known limits:** 40 of the 58 Gemini notes docs attached to calendar events returned not found for miko@ (originals not shared), so folder or shared-drive copies were used. The 20 Jul 2026 client meeting 'Wagertech <> Jumpr: Deal Rep Assignment' (5 attendees) has no notes doc or transcript, so its decisions are not in the ledger. 8 docs are empty placeholders (8, 10, 11, 22, 29 Sep and 2 Oct Internal Syncs, 16 Sep Redeposits Discovery, 2 Oct CMS Integration Sync), and the 30 Sep Internal Sync is a 51-second recording with no content. Tier 2 internal delivery-team notes (52 docs) are used as corroboration only; client decisions rest on the 47 Tier 1 meetings. 18 of the 99 ledger docs are Gemini notes only, with no verbatim transcript, so evidence from them is a summary rather than spoken words. Jira was pulled as a snapshot on 2026-10-03 (505 WAGR issues); verifiers re-read live Jira only for the 116 sampled claims, so later changes to other tickets are not reflected. Where no Jira key was spoken, transcript items were matched to tickets by meaning, so some matches are judgement calls. The ledger ends on 30 Sep 2026 because both 2 Oct docs are empty, so anything decided after 30 Sep is not covered. The verification sample was all 95 High and Medium claims plus every 5th Low (21 of 101), so 78 Low items in the final register were not independently verified.

- **What differs:** Jira builds Signup Currency as a formula from the Player's country/CurrencyIsoCode. The 8/27 client session decided the sign-up payout currency defaults from the Deal's market country (Canada=CAD, US=USD), is stamped on the Sign-Up (not a player formula, because of relocation cases) and stays editable by Ops. No ticket implements the Deal-market-country default.
- **Suggested action:** Confirm with Emily which rule is current (8/27 deal-market-country stamp vs the 9/18 Slack-agreed player-country formula). If 8/27 stands, add a story for the Deal-market-country default on Sign-Up and update WAGR-404/WAGR-160. Note WAGR-415: most SLCs arrive without player country, so a player-country rule falls back to CAD.
- **Confidence:** medium · **Verifier note:** The gap is real but the claim frames it wrongly. The 8/27 decision has two parts: Sign-Up currency defaults from the Deal market country (L2125/L2138/L2139), and Player currency defaults from Player country (L2145/L2146). WAGR-404, WAGR-160 and the 9/18 change (L2704) are all about the Player-level Signup Currency field, so they match the 8/27 Player decision and do not contradict it. What is actually missing is a ticket to default Sign_Up__c.Signup_Currency__c (created in WAGR-7) from the Deal market country, stamped on the record and editable by Ops. No WAGR ticket covers that. I lowered severity to Medium because separate payout currency work is deferred to payouts discovery (L2140; WAGR-465 is in Requirements).

## 6. Gemini summary vs transcript disagreements found during extraction

364 disagreements across 40 docs. Pattern: the Gemini 'Decisions'/'Summary' sections state as agreed what the transcript shows as proposed, split, or client-asked-only.

- **2026-05-27 — Jumpr <> WagerTech: Salesforce PRD Review** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ha5oDS_JGfc-esDrrTVH_KnFVlX5hAYUzSz7dVUOmo4/edit), line 369): Summary says: "Standard Salesforce objects prioritized Standard Salesforce objects are prioritized over custom objects for the new implementation, defaulting to native features whenever possible. [listed under Decisions: ALIGNED]; also Summary: 'A decision was made to prioritize standard functionality over custom " — Transcript: "Waleed Alasadi: Okay. Me and I are split, so we don't have a hard opinion yet, / Waleed Alasadi: we don't think that you should use custom objects. Um but we're like we're going to determine throughout the process. Okay." — Summary marks this as an aligned decision; transcript shows a Jumpr stance with no hard opinion yet, to be determined during discovery, and no client confirmation.
- **2026-05-27 — Jumpr <> WagerTech: Salesforce PRD Review** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ha5oDS_JGfc-esDrrTVH_KnFVlX5hAYUzSz7dVUOmo4/edit), line 398): Summary says: "Partners and Operators as Accounts Partners and Operators are to be implemented as standard Salesforce Account objects to enable effective contact relationship tracking. [Decisions: ALIGNED]; Details: 'The consultants also determined that "Partners" and "Operators" should be treated as Accounts'" — Transcript: "Waleed Alasadi: accounts like full-on like accounts and we'll use them simply because you have to use um the contacts under there. / Joyce Kiddell: Mhm. / Waleed Alasadi: Um, so that's like one answer on native that we'll kind of look into." — Summary hardens a direction Jumpr said it will 'look into' into an aligned decision; client gave only 'Mhm'.
- **2026-05-27 — Jumpr <> WagerTech: Salesforce PRD Review** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ha5oDS_JGfc-esDrrTVH_KnFVlX5hAYUzSz7dVUOmo4/edit), line 477): Summary says: "External file linking strategy adopted The file storage strategy will prioritize saving links to external files (e.g., Dropbox, Drive) instead of uploading raw files to Salesforce to optimize storage costs." — Transcript: "Waleed Alasadi: that works with like you put in so instead of like uploading the file, / Waleed Alasadi: you put a link to the file and call it a day that way." — Summary says the strategy was adopted; transcript has a Jumpr suggestion with no explicit client confirmation, and Snowflake was still being checked as an option.
- **2026-05-27 — Jumpr <> WagerTech: Salesforce PRD Review** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ha5oDS_JGfc-esDrrTVH_KnFVlX5hAYUzSz7dVUOmo4/edit), line 242): Summary says: "The team aligned on structuring data for reporting to support Cost Per Acquisition tracking." — Transcript: "do we need to have a sense of market as its own thing or is it just attached to deals for example? / the problem with multi-state pick list is it won't give you the pivoting that you're looking for when it comes to reporting" — No alignment on how market data is structured was reached; Waleed only described the limitation of multi-select picklists. Summary is firmer than transcript.
- **2026-05-27 — Jumpr <> WagerTech: Salesforce PRD Review** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ha5oDS_JGfc-esDrrTVH_KnFVlX5hAYUzSz7dVUOmo4/edit), line 313): Summary says: "Joyce Kiddell and Lina Ceniccola confirmed that because deal origination occurs in a single location, the team does not need to split amounts by percentage at the signup level" — Transcript: "Lina Ceniccola: So it's always related to that that actual signup wherever it originated if that makes / Waleed Alasadi: that that's that makes sense because the origination is a single place which like we don't have to split any amounts by like Yeah. by any percentages." — Transcript ties single-location origination to the signup (where the player signs up from), not to deal origination; deals can span multiple markets. Summary misattributes.
- **2026-05-28 — Jumpr: Discovery (WagerTech end-user process walkthrough)** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/153GXa2Bxzi2tRciqHschinynA20rOR89xr4fkYer7_o/edit), line 965): Summary says: "Leadership decided to integrate WhatsApp communications directly into Salesforce to streamline administrative logging tasks." — Transcript: "Joyce Kiddell: Uh yeah, that that can come later / Joyce Kiddell: potentially. / Joyce Kiddell: Okay, great. Yeah, feel free to um build it into the recommendation. / Joyce Kiddell: Um but we can talk about like sequencing and and where that would make sense." — Summary is firmer. Joyce only agreed to include WhatsApp in Jumpr's recommendation, with sequencing to be discussed; earlier she said it 'can come later potentially'. No decision to integrate was made.
- **2026-05-28 — Jumpr: Discovery (WagerTech end-user process walkthrough)** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/153GXa2Bxzi2tRciqHschinynA20rOR89xr4fkYer7_o/edit), line 632): Summary says: "[Waleed Alasadi] Build AI Extraction: Develop an automated AI process to extract metadata such as sign up and deposit timestamps from player screenshots." — Transcript: "Joyce Kiddell: Um I'm not sure if like that would have to be you guys building the AI extraction piece of it, but it's something that we've already kind of discussed / Waleed Alasadi: Yeah, we can. / Um yeah, we don't have to. I think like right now phase one is about building the the the infrastruc" — Summary turns a client wish into a Jumpr-owned action item. Joyce was unsure who would build it; Waleed said Jumpr can but does not have to and that phase one is infrastructure. No owner was assigned.
- **2026-05-28 — Jumpr: Discovery (WagerTech end-user process walkthrough)** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/153GXa2Bxzi2tRciqHschinynA20rOR89xr4fkYer7_o/edit), line 812): Summary says: "[Jay] Detail Tactics Process: Provide a high level summary of the Tactics platform and its workflows to support future system integration." — Transcript: "Joyce Kiddell: process. So maybe you can speak to it like kind of high level, but um I'm not sure if we'll have it in the initial build out yet. / Joyce Kiddell: but anyway, yeah, just go through it high level." — Joyce asked Jay to speak to TT at high level during the meeting, and he did. It was not a follow-up action, and TT in the initial build was left uncertain.
- **2026-05-28 — Jumpr: Discovery (WagerTech end-user process walkthrough)** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/153GXa2Bxzi2tRciqHschinynA20rOR89xr4fkYer7_o/edit), line 381): Summary says: "Deal management functionality moved to Salesforce The deal management functionality, currently handled via external spreadsheets, will be integrated into the Salesforce implementation." — Transcript: "work right um that we're also hoping to bring into Salesforce." — Summary is firmer ('will be integrated', listed as ALIGNED decision); Joyce said they are 'hoping to bring' it into Salesforce. Also the source is AirTable, not only spreadsheets.
- **2026-05-28 — Jumpr: Discovery (WagerTech end-user process walkthrough)** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/153GXa2Bxzi2tRciqHschinynA20rOR89xr4fkYer7_o/edit), line 912): Summary says: "The company identifies priority books—such as DraftKings, CTM, and Proline—for referral payments to maximize the benefit for the business." — Transcript: "Uh so that's why uh it's primarily DraftKing CTM Proline C here a little bit of BMGMGD and then a few odd ones but for the most part we decide what books they are." — Summary splits book names: the priority books are 'DraftKings CTM' and 'Proline C' (operator + affiliate suffix), not DraftKings, CTM and Proline as three books. Matters for the deal = operator + partner model.
- **2026-06-03 — Jumpr - Wagertech Next Steps** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CiCF1Kmv2QPJOeKn7mRRoUY1G-tldtZ1rdeomsW_Cp8/edit), line 142): Summary says: "WhatsApp selected for notifications The team decided to utilize WhatsApp for system notifications instead of the native Salesforce app or email." — Transcript: "Joyce Kiddell: ... maybe that like we pivot that to just be like WhatsApp focused. / Waleed Alasadi: So and that that could happen absolutely like notifications to WhatsApp could happen." — Summary marks it ALIGNED/decided; transcript shows a tentative suggestion ('maybe') and 'could happen', with WhatsApp work also deferred out of Phase 1.
- **2026-06-03 — Jumpr - Wagertech Next Steps** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CiCF1Kmv2QPJOeKn7mRRoUY1G-tldtZ1rdeomsW_Cp8/edit), line 159): Summary says: "Dedicated WhatsApp Business account required The team committed to acquiring a dedicated WhatsApp Business account to handle notification delivery." — Transcript: "Lina Ceniccola: Yeah, we could get a WhatsApp business account dedicated to this." — Summary says 'committed'; Lina only said they 'could' get one.
- **2026-06-03 — Jumpr - Wagertech Next Steps** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CiCF1Kmv2QPJOeKn7mRRoUY1G-tldtZ1rdeomsW_Cp8/edit), line 167): Summary says: "Object model design approach accepted The team accepted the proposed object model design, which includes utilizing Person Accounts for players and referrers and the native User object for role management." — Transcript: "Waleed Alasadi: So, we can talk more about like this is not final. Obviously, in the first like week or so, we're going to finalize the design." — Summary says accepted; Waleed said it is not final, and Joyce later asked that the data engineer's ERD be the source of truth with the data engineer owning the final design.
- **2026-06-03 — Jumpr - Wagertech Next Steps** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CiCF1Kmv2QPJOeKn7mRRoUY1G-tldtZ1rdeomsW_Cp8/edit), line 224): Summary says: "Phased project delivery targets a late July launch to ensure high quality outcomes." — Transcript: "Waleed Alasadi: I know you mentioned middle of July. It is really tight ... I think July 31st or end of July. / Joyce Kiddell: ... maybe give us like an updated like more realistic timeline" — No launch target was agreed. Client asked for mid-July, Jumpr proposed end of July and then suggested going beyond July; an updated timeline is pending in the follow-up email.
- **2026-06-03 — Jumpr - Wagertech Next Steps** ([doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CiCF1Kmv2QPJOeKn7mRRoUY1G-tldtZ1rdeomsW_Cp8/edit), line 391): Summary says: "[Joyce Kiddell, Lina Ceniccola] Develop Internal Skills: Support Eric in completing Salesforce administrator training through the Trailhead system." — Transcript: "Waleed Alasadi: Okay.
